slides.title: Coverage isn't *capacity*.
slides.body:
Green in every corner.
The complaints keep arriving.

slides.title: A radio is a shared medium
slides.body:
One device talks at a time.
Everyone else *waits their turn*.

slides.title: Forty devices, one conversation
slides.body:
Not forty conversations.
One — taken in turns, very quickly.

slides.title: The slowest client sets the tax
slides.body:
A device at the edge negotiates a low rate and holds the medium *longer* for the same data.
Slow for everyone on that radio.

slides.title: The map answers the wrong question
slides.body:
“Did signal reach here.”
The complaint is *“did I get a turn.”*

slides.title: Look at these instead
slides.body:
Channel utilization. Retry rate.
Clients per radio at *peak*.
The data rates in use.

slides.title: More power makes it worse
slides.body:
Bigger cells → more clients per radio → more overlap.
The heat map gets greener while the experience *degrades*.

slides.title: Capacity is the design.
slides.body:
Coverage is a design input.
A heat map tells you the signal arrived — not that the user got a turn to speak.
